actionRationale: Peak attention has passed, competition is high, and I found no purchase-intent evidence. Reconsider only if trend data shows a rebound.

adopters.text: Mainly children, teens and Gen Z, with heavy use in schools. Teachers and schools reacted, and some banned it. Brands such as Buc-ee's and Southwest Airlines joined in.

competition.text: Etsy has many 6-7 listings, including PNG design bundles, sweatshirts and embroidered shirts. Walmart and Buc-ee's also carry products. I could not count listings.

gap.text: No clear gap is visible. Existing listings already cover tees, PNG bundles and gifts. Any remaining angle, such as teacher classroom humor printables, would target a fading trend. This is an inference, not an observation.

name: 6-7 (Six Seven) meme

origin.text: Rapper Skrilla released 'Doot Doot' on 2024-12-01, with the line '6-7' reportedly referring to 67th Street in Philadelphia. TikTok edits of LaMelo Ball (listed at 6 ft 7 in) popularized it through 2025.

productDemand.text: Many 6-7 products are listed on Etsy, and Buc-ee's sells a 67 T-shirt. These are supply, not demand. I found no sales figures, sell-outs or purchase-intent surveys.

rights.note: Skrilla's song and lyrics, LaMelo Ball's name and likeness, and brand marks (e.g. Buc-ee's) should be avoided. The bare number is generic, but I did not find trademark status either way.

buyerIntent.rationale: Brand merch exists but no sales or purchase-intent evidence was found.

durability.rationale: Described as declining; brainrot memes are typically short-lived (inference).

economics.rationale: Low cost to produce, but high competition and a shrinking window.

productFit.rationale: A text-based meme suits tees, stickers and digital PNG bundles, and each is quick to make.

supplyGap.rationale: Etsy and big retailers already supply the obvious products.

timing.rationale: Reports of decline in 2026 after the late-2025 peak.

spread.text: It spread well beyond its source: sports edits, then school culture, then brands and dictionaries. Searches reportedly rose sixfold by June 2025.

summary: A nonsensical Gen Z/Gen Alpha catchphrase and hand gesture from Skrilla's 'Doot Doot (6 7)' and LaMelo Ball edits, named Dictionary.com's 2025 Word of the Year and now reported to be declining.

trajectory.text: Dictionary.com named it Word of the Year in late 2025, which marks the peak of mainstream attention. 2026 snippets say it is 'in a decline in popularity' and has become 'no longer trendy'. One snippet says it is still going strong among younger kids, so evidence is mixed. I could not read the pages or any trend data.

unresolved: No trend data (Google Trends, TikTok) read
what: '6-7' is a meaningless, ironic interjection, often paired with a shrug-like hand gesture. It is used for 'so-so' or 'maybe' and in jokes such as scoring 67% on an exam. It spread from basketball edits to school playgrounds and mainstream brands. Dictionary.com classed it as brainrot.

invalidators: A new viral revival or a related event, such as a sports moment or brand campaign
window.reasoning: Reported decline in 2026 and a POD delivery time of 1-2 weeks plus weeks for a new listing to be discovered leave little time to earn from it. I cannot give a dated estimate from the available evidence.
window.seasonality: School-year humor; no fixed deadline found.
